title: Admin - Assign Permissions to Limited Access Admin - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Assign Permissions to Limited Access Admin feature on the Y4J platform. This feature provides a permissions checklist (User Management, Vendor Management, Product Approval, Content Management, Content Moderation, Comment Management, Analytics, System Settings) with selectable checkboxes. At least one permission must be selected. Selected permissions are saved with the admin record and displayed on the admin card. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for checkbox group accessibility, keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility, validation, and dynamic content.

testCases.title: Permissions checkbox group has accessible group label
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Add/Edit Internal Admin form is open with Limited-Access Admin role selected, permissions section is visible
steps: Navigate to the permissions section using screen reader
Verify the group of checkboxes has a group label (via <fieldset>/<legend> or role='group' with aria-label/aria-labelledby)
Verify screen reader announces the group name (e.g., 'Permissions' or 'Assign Permissions')
Verify the group label clearly describes the purpose
expectedResults: Permissions checkboxes are wrapped in a <fieldset> with <legend>, or a container with role='group' and aria-label
Screen reader announces the group label when entering the group (e.g., 'Permissions, group')
Group label clearly communicates the purpose of the checkboxes
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users understand the context of the checkbox group

testCases.title: Each permission checkbox has an accessible label
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Navigate to each permission checkbox using Tab or screen reader
Verify 'User Management' checkbox has accessible label
Verify 'Vendor Management' checkbox has accessible label
Verify 'Product Approval' checkbox has accessible label
Verify 'Content Management' checkbox has accessible label
Verify 'Content Moderation' checkbox has accessible label
Verify 'Comment Management' checkbox has accessible label
Verify 'Analytics' checkbox has accessible label
Verify 'System Settings' checkbox has accessible label
expectedResults: Each checkbox has a programmatically associated label (via <label for>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby)
Screen reader announces each checkbox with its name and role (e.g., 'User Management, checkbox, not checked')
Clicking/tapping the label text toggles the checkbox
All 8 permissions have unique, descriptive labels
testCases.postconditions: All permission checkboxes are properly labeled

testCases.title: Checkboxes are operable via keyboard
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Tab to the first permission checkbox
Press Space to check the checkbox
Verify the checkbox becomes checked
Press Space again to uncheck
Verify the checkbox becomes unchecked
Tab to the next checkbox
Repeat for all 8 checkboxes
expectedResults: Each checkbox is reachable via Tab key
Space key toggles the checked/unchecked state
Checked state is visually indicated
Screen reader announces state change ('checked' / 'not checked')
No mouse interaction is required
testCases.postconditions: All checkboxes are fully operable via keyboard

testCases.title: Checkbox checked/unchecked state is announced by screen reader
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Navigate to an unchecked permission checkbox with screen reader
Verify screen reader announces 'not checked' state
Press Space to check the checkbox
Verify screen reader announces 'checked' state
Press Space to uncheck
Verify screen reader announces 'not checked' state again
expectedResults: Screen reader announces 'checkbox, not checked' for unchecked state
Screen reader announces 'checkbox, checked' after checking
State change is announced immediately upon toggle
Both native checkboxes and custom ARIA checkboxes communicate state correctly
testCases.postconditions: Checkbox state is always communicated to assistive technology

testCases.title: Checkboxes have visible focus indicators
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Tab to the first permission checkbox
Observe the focus indicator
Tab through all 8 checkboxes
Verify each shows a visible focus indicator
expectedResults: Each checkbox shows a clearly visible focus indicator when focused
Focus indicator has at least 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors
Focus indicator is not solely a color change
Focus indicator is distinguishable from the checked state indicator
testCases.postconditions: Focus state is clearly visible on all checkboxes

testCases.title: No permission selected validation error is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible, no checkboxes are checked
steps: Ensure no permission checkboxes are checked
Attempt to save/submit the admin form
Verify an error message is displayed indicating at least one permission is required
Verify the error is announced by screen reader
Verify the error is programmatically associated with the permissions group
Verify focus moves to the permissions section or error message
expectedResults: Error message is displayed (e.g., 'At least one permission must be selected')
Error is announced by screen reader (via role='alert', aria-live='assertive', or focus management)
Error is associated with the permissions group (aria-describedby on the group or aria-errormessage)
The permissions group or first checkbox has aria-invalid='true'
Focus moves to the error or the permissions section
testCases.postconditions: Users are clearly informed that at least one permission is required

testCases.title: Error suggestion provides guidance for no permission selected
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, no permissions selected, form submitted
steps: Submit the form with no permissions selected
Read the error message text
Verify the message suggests how to fix the issue
expectedResults: Error message clearly states the requirement (e.g., 'Please select at least one permission to assign to this admin')
Message is constructive and guides the user to correct the issue
Message does not use technical jargon
testCases.postconditions: Users receive helpful guidance to fix the validation error

testCases.title: Permission list failure shows accessible error notification
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, API for permissions list is configured to fail
steps: Navigate to the permissions section when the API fails to load permissions
Verify an error message is displayed
Verify the error uses role='alert' or aria-live='assertive'
Verify screen reader immediately announces the error
Verify the error does not rely solely on color
expectedResults: Error notification is visually displayed (e.g., 'Failed to load permissions. Please try again.')
Screen reader immediately announces the error
Error includes text (not just a colored indicator)
Error text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
A retry mechanism is available and accessible
testCases.postconditions: Permission load failure is communicated to all users

testCases.title: Tab order through permissions is logical
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible with all 8 checkboxes
steps: Tab to the first permission checkbox
Continue tabbing through all checkboxes
Document the tab order
Verify the order matches the visual layout (top-to-bottom or left-to-right)
expectedResults: Tab order follows: User Management → Vendor Management → Product Approval → Content Management → Content Moderation → Comment Management → Analytics → System Settings
Order matches the visual presentation
No checkboxes are skipped
No unexpected focus jumps
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard navigation through permissions is predictable

testCases.title: No keyboard trap in permissions section
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Tab into the permissions checkbox group
Tab through all checkboxes
Continue tabbing past the last checkbox
Verify focus moves to the next element outside the group (e.g., Save/Add Admin button)
Shift+Tab back into the permissions group
Verify focus returns to the last checkbox
expectedResults: Focus enters and exits the permissions group freely
Tab moves past the last checkbox to the next interactive element
Shift+Tab returns to the permissions group from the next element
No keyboard trap exists within the checkbox group
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard users can freely navigate in and out of permissions

testCases.title: Checkbox labels have sufficient color contrast
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Use a contrast checker tool
Measure contrast of each permission label text against its background
Check contrast of checked checkbox indicator against background
Check contrast of unchecked checkbox border against background
expectedResults: All label text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against background
Checked checkbox indicator (checkmark) has at least 3:1 contrast against checkbox background
Unchecked checkbox border has at least 3:1 contrast against surrounding background
All text is readable for users with low vision
testCases.postconditions: All permission labels and checkboxes are visually accessible

testCases.title: Checked state does not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, some permissions are checked and some unchecked
steps: Check some permission checkboxes and leave others unchecked
Observe the visual difference between checked and unchecked states
View the page in grayscale mode
Verify checked and unchecked states are still distinguishable
expectedResults: Checked state uses more than color alone (e.g., checkmark icon, filled background, border change)
In grayscale mode, checked and unchecked states are clearly distinguishable
Visual indicator is clear and unambiguous
testCases.postconditions: Checkbox states are perceivable regardless of color vision

testCases.title: Permissions section is functional at 200% browser zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify all 8 permission checkboxes and labels are visible
Verify labels are not clipped or overlapping
Check/uncheck checkboxes and verify functionality
Verify error messages (if triggered) are visible
expectedResults: All 8 checkboxes and labels are fully visible at 200% zoom
No text is clipped or hidden
Checkboxes remain clickable/tappable
Labels do not overlap checkboxes or each other
Layout adapts appropriately (may stack vertically)
testCases.postconditions: Permissions section is fully functional at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Permissions section reflows at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify all permission checkboxes are accessible without horizontal scrolling
Verify labels are fully readable
Check/uncheck checkboxes and verify functionality
expectedResults: Permissions reflow to single column if needed
No horizontal scrollbar required
All labels are fully readable without truncation
Checkboxes remain functional at narrow width
testCases.postconditions: Permissions work on narrow viewports

testCases.title: Checkbox touch targets meet minimum size
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section viewed on touch device
steps: Measure the clickable/tappable area of each permission checkbox (including label)
Verify adequate spacing between checkboxes
Verify checkboxes are not too close together for accidental activation
expectedResults: Each checkbox + label combination has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
Adequate vertical spacing exists between checkbox rows
No accidental activation of adjacent checkboxes
testCases.postconditions: Checkboxes are usable for users with motor impairments

testCases.title: Saved permissions are displayed accessibly on admin card
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, an admin has been created with specific permissions assigned
steps: Navigate to the admin list and find the admin card with assigned permissions
Verify permissions are displayed on the card
Navigate to the permissions display using screen reader
Verify screen reader announces the permissions with a label (e.g., 'Assigned permissions: User Management, Analytics')
Verify the permissions list uses semantic markup
expectedResults: Permissions are visually displayed on the admin card
Permissions have a descriptive label (e.g., 'Assigned Permissions')
Screen reader announces the label and permission values
If displayed as a list, semantic list markup is used
Permissions text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
testCases.postconditions: Saved permissions are accessible on the admin card

testCases.title: Selecting all permissions provides informational feedback
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Check all 8 permission checkboxes
Observe if any informational message appears (e.g., 'All permissions selected - equivalent to Super Admin')
If a message appears, verify it is announced by screen reader
Verify the message uses aria-live='polite' or role='status'
expectedResults: If informational message is shown, it is accessible to screen readers
Message uses aria-live='polite' (informational, not critical)
Message does not prevent form submission
Message text has sufficient contrast
testCases.postconditions: Users are informed about the implication of selecting all permissions

testCases.title: Permission save confirmation is announced accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions have been selected and form is submitted
steps: Select one or more permissions
Submit/save the admin form
Verify a success message is displayed or announced
Verify screen reader announces the success
Verify the admin card shows the saved permissions
expectedResults: Success is communicated (via toast/notification with role='status' or aria-live='polite')
Screen reader announces success (e.g., 'Permissions saved successfully')
Admin card displays the assigned permissions
Focus returns to an appropriate element
testCases.postconditions: Successful permission save is communicated to all users

testCases.title: Error state on validation does not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, no permissions selected, form submitted to trigger error
steps: Submit the form with no permissions selected
Observe how the error state is indicated on the permissions section
View in grayscale mode
Verify the error is still identifiable without color
expectedResults: Error includes text message (not just red border around checkboxes)
Error has an icon or text prefix in addition to color
In grayscale mode, error state is still clearly identifiable
Error uses multiple visual cues (text + border + icon)
testCases.postconditions: Validation errors are perceivable regardless of color vision

testCases.title: Permissions section is within appropriate landmark and has heading
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, permissions section is visible
steps: Use screen reader heading navigation to find the permissions section
Verify the section has a heading or is within a labeled region
Verify the section is within the main landmark or dialog
Verify the heading level follows the page hierarchy
expectedResults: Permissions section has a heading (e.g., H3 'Permissions') or is a labeled region
Section is within the main landmark or modal dialog
Heading level is appropriate in the hierarchy (not skipping levels)
Screen reader users can navigate directly to the permissions section
testCases.postconditions: Permissions section is structurally discoverable
